correctness.rationale: For fixed C³ periodic f, support function h_delta(theta)=1+delta f(theta) yields for small delta>=0 a strictly convex C² boundary. Diameter D_delta=max_u[h(u)+h(-u)]=2+delta M, M=max H(theta), H=f(theta)+f(theta+pi). Uniform implicit-function boundary intersections near central offsets t=0 give L_delta(theta,t)=2-t²+delta H(theta)+O_f(t⁴+delta |t|+delta²) at all angles. When epsilon->0 and delta/epsilon->finite x, comparison to enclosing concentric disks localizes L>D−epsilon to |t|=O(sqrt epsilon); normalized indicator tends to z²+x(M−H(theta))<1. The Crofton line normalization is P_delta->2pi; dominated convergence produces G_f(x)=pi^(-1) integral sqrt((1−xDelta(theta))_+) dtheta. For constant H, G=1; for nonconstant continuous H it is strictly decreasing; isolated nondegenerate maxima yield G(x)~(2 sqrt x)^(-1) sum sqrt(2/(-H(theta_j))). Independently checked exact ellipse chord integral against G(x) for x=0,.5,1,3,12 at epsilon=1e-4 (differences <1.3e-4). This is only a finite x double-limit theorem; no uniform assertion for diverging delta/epsilon.

Bäsel 2012 gives explicit fixed regular-polygon chord laws; Martirosyan 2023 covers quadrilateral orientation-dependent chords. None of the inspected available statements supplies this near-circle crossover profile or its antipodal-width dependence. Gates full text remains inaccessible (Oxford VPN disconnected), so best-of-knowledge PASS qualified by nontrivial priority risk; fixed-shape density novelty is expressly disclaimed.
